keyTakeaways: Ten October dates (2, 3, 9, 10, 16, 17, 23, 24, 30, 31) are a Friday, Saturday or Sunday in both 2026 and 2027, so the calendar's longest films sit there.
The 12 dates that are Monday to Thursday in both years carry films averaging 76 minutes; the whole calendar runs 2,624 minutes, about 43.7 hours.
Six silent films from 1920 to 1928 are US public domain now; Dracula and Frankenstein (1931) join them on 1 January 2027.
AFI's history note says Night of the Living Dead regained a copyright in 1986, so its public-domain status is disputed.
48.3% of views of SubhSandesh shared pages are on a phone, so each night is written as one screenshot-sized line.

faqs.question: When does the 31 days of Halloween movies challenge start?
faqs.answer: It starts on 1 October and ends on 31 October, one film a night. 1 October is a Thursday in 2026 and a Friday in 2027, so the first weekend arrives after one night in 2026 and immediately in 2027.

faqs.question: What should I watch on Halloween night itself?
faqs.answer: Halloween (1978), directed by John Carpenter, runs 93 minutes and is set on Halloween night. The Library of Congress added it to the National Film Registry in 2006, and 31 October falls on a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027.

faqs.question: Do I have to watch the films in this exact order?
faqs.answer: No. The theme weeks are a suggestion, but if you swap two films, move anything over 95 minutes only onto the 2nd, 3rd, 9th, 10th, 16th, 17th, 23rd, 24th, 30th or 31st, the dates that are weekends in both 2026 and 2027.

faqs.question: Is Night of the Living Dead really public domain?
faqs.answer: It is widely listed that way, and archive.org hosts copies marked public domain. The AFI Catalog's history note, citing Variety from 1990, says the film lost its copyright when it was retitled but that Image Ten secured a new copyright in 1986, so its status is less settled than most lists say.

faqs.question: How many hours does it take to watch all 31 films?
faqs.answer: About 43.7 hours, or 2,624 minutes, which averages 85 minutes a night. The shortest night is The Fall of the House of Usher at 13 minutes and the longest is Bedknobs and Broomsticks at 117.

faqs.question: Can kids do a Halloween movie calendar?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only part of this one. Family week, 19 to 24 October, has films AFI rates G, PG and one PG-13, while weeks 3 and 5 include 8 films rated R.

faqs.question: Where can I stream these Halloween movies?
faqs.answer: The six silent films have copies on archive.org. For the rest, streaming catalogues change monthly and differ by country, so search each title in a JustWatch-type tracker on the day you watch.

faqs.question: Is one movie a night better than a horror marathon?
faqs.answer: Research on TV series suggests so. A 2017 study of 51 students found one-sitting viewers enjoyed a show less and forgot it faster than daily or weekly viewers, and a 2017 survey of 423 young adults linked frequent binge viewing to poorer sleep.

faqs.question: Which October dates are weekends in both 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: The 2nd, 3rd, 9th, 10th, 16th, 17th, 23rd, 24th, 30th and 31st fall on a Friday, Saturday or Sunday in both years. This calendar puts its longest films on those ten dates.

faqs.question: Can I send someone the movie calendar as a Halloween surprise?
faqs.answer: You can send the plan inside a Halloween greeting page for one person, with photos, a letter and, on the premium page, a voice note and an unlock time. It cannot stream or sync a film, so treat it as the invitation, not the screening.

article.contentMarkdown:
# 31 Days of Halloween Movies: A Weekday-Aware October Calendar

This 31 days of Halloween movies calendar gives you one film a night from 1 to 31 October, in five theme weeks that end with *Halloween* (1978) on the 31st. Two SubhSandesh numbers shaped it: 48.3% of the 57,456 views of pages shared on our platform were on a phone, so each night is one line you can screenshot, and on Raksha Bandhan 2026, our nearest festival analogue (89 pages, a small sample), 49.4% of pages were built on the day itself, so you can join late.

The schedule follows the real weekdays: 1 October is a Thursday in 2026 and a Friday in 2027. Ten dates (2, 3, 9, 10, 16, 17, 23, 24, 30 and 31) fall on a Friday, Saturday or Sunday in both years, so the longest films sit there, while the 12 dates that are Monday to Thursday in both years average 76 minutes.

## What is a 31 days of Halloween movies calendar?

A 31 days of Halloween movies calendar, also searched as a Halloween movie calendar, assigns one horror or Halloween film to each night of October. It swaps one marathon weekend for a nightly habit of 13 to 117 minutes.

This version adds an order. Films climb by era inside five theme weeks, and the scares drop for family week (19 to 24 October) before the adults-only finale.

## The 31 films, 1–31 October, week by week

Weekdays are shown as 2026 / 2027, and years and directors come from the AFI Catalog, the National Film Registry or archive.org records. Runtimes are AFI's (the longer where it gives two) or the archive.org copy's, since silents vary with projection speed.

### Week 1, 1–6 October: the silent era

All six were published before 1931, which puts them in the US public domain. They run on images and music rather than dialogue, and 6 October is a 13-minute short.

- **1 Oct (Thu / Fri):** *The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari* (1920; archive.org says 1919), Robert Wiene, about 72 min.
- **2 Oct (Fri / Sat):** *Nosferatu* (1922), F. W. Murnau, 93 min in the most complete archive.org copy.
- **3 Oct (Sat / Sun):** *The Phantom of the Opera* (1925), Rupert Julian, 107 min.
- **4 Oct (Sun / Mon):** *The Cat and the Canary* (1927), Paul Leni, about 87 min.
- **5 Oct (Mon / Tue):** *Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde* (1920), John S. Robertson, 79 min.
- **6 Oct (Tue / Wed):** *The Fall of the House of Usher* (1928), J. S. Watson and M. Webber, 13 min, on the National Film Registry since 2000.

### Week 2, 7–13 October: Universal monsters

Universal's cycle is the easiest weeknight theme, because AFI lists all seven at 80 minutes or under. In release order, the monsters go on to meet their sequels.

- **7 Oct (Wed / Thu):** *Dracula* (1931), Tod Browning, 75 min.
- **8 Oct (Thu / Fri):** *Frankenstein* (1931), James Whale, 70 min.
- **9 Oct (Fri / Sat):** *The Mummy* (1932), Karl Freund, 78 min.
- **10 Oct (Sat / Sun):** *The Invisible Man* (1933), James Whale, 71 min.
- **11 Oct (Sun / Mon):** *Bride of Frankenstein* (1935), James Whale, 80 min.
- **12 Oct (Mon / Tue):** *The Wolf Man* (1941), George Waggner, 70 min.
- **13 Oct (Tue / Wed):** *Creature from the Black Lagoon* (1954), Jack Arnold, 79 min.

### Week 3, 14–18 October: folk horror

Folk horror puts the threat in a place and its beliefs: a village, a cornfield, a curse. The two films over 90 minutes take 16 and 17 October, a weekend in both years.

- **14 Oct (Wed / Thu):** *Village of the Damned* (1960), Wolf Rilla, 78 min.
- **15 Oct (Thu / Fri):** *Curse of the Demon* (1958), Jacques Tourneur, 82 min.
- **16 Oct (Fri / Sat):** *Halloween III: Season of the Witch* (1982), Tommy Lee Wallace, 98 min.
- **17 Oct (Sat / Sun):** *Children of the Corn* (1984), Fritz Kiersch, 93 min.
- **18 Oct (Sun / Mon):** *Let's Scare Jessica to Death* (1971), John Hancock, 89 min.

### Week 4, 19–24 October: family week

Week 4 drops the R ratings so children can join. AFI lists *Bedknobs and Broomsticks* as G, *The Watcher in the Woods* and *Little Monsters* as PG, and *The Monster Squad* as PG-13, so preview that one for under-13s.

- **19 Oct (Mon / Tue):** *Bud Abbott and Lou Costello Meet Frankenstein* (1948), Charles T. Barton, 83 min, week 2's monsters as comedy.
- **20 Oct (Tue / Wed):** *The Monster Squad* (1987), Fred Dekker, 82 min.
- **21 Oct (Wed / Thu):** *The Watcher in the Woods* (1981), John Hough, 83 min.
- **22 Oct (Thu / Fri):** *Mad Monster Party* (1969), Jules Bass, 94 min, stop-motion.
- **23 Oct (Fri / Sat):** *Bedknobs and Broomsticks* (1971), Robert Stevenson, 117 min, the longest film here.
- **24 Oct (Sat / Sun):** *Little Monsters* (1989), Richard Alan Greenberg, 102 min.

### Week 5, 25–31 October: modern horror

The finale runs from 1968 to 2015, and AFI lists six of the seven as R. The one long film on a weeknight is *It Follows* on Thursday 29 October 2026, so start it by 8 pm that year.

- **25 Oct (Sun / Mon):** *Night of the Living Dead* (1968), George A. Romero, 90 min.
- **26 Oct (Mon / Tue):** *The Fog* (1980), John Carpenter, 90 min.
- **27 Oct (Tue / Wed):** *Night of the Demons* (1988), Kevin S. Tenney, 89 min.
- **28 Oct (Wed / Thu):** *Pumpkinhead* (1989), Stan Winston, 86 min.
- **29 Oct (Thu / Fri):** *It Follows* (2015), David Robert Mitchell, 100 min.
- **30 Oct (Fri / Sat):** *Candyman* (1992), Bernard Rose, 101 min.
- **31 Oct (Sat / Sun):** *Halloween* (1978), John Carpenter, 93 min, set on Halloween night and on the National Film Registry since 2006.

## The five weeks compared

The table totals each week's runtimes. The full calendar runs 2,624 minutes, about 43.7 hours or 85 minutes a night.

| Week (dates) | Films, total minutes | Longest film | US public domain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Silent era (1–6 Oct) | 6 films, 451 min | *The Phantom of the Opera*, 107 min | 6 of 6 |
| Universal monsters (7–13 Oct) | 7 films, 523 min | *Bride of Frankenstein*, 80 min | 0 in 2026; 2 from 1 Jan 2027 |
| Folk horror (14–18 Oct) | 5 films, 440 min | *Halloween III*, 98 min | 0 |
| Family (19–24 Oct) | 6 films, 561 min | *Bedknobs and Broomsticks*, 117 min | 0 |
| Modern (25–31 Oct) | 7 films, 649 min | *Candyman*, 101 min | 1 disputed |

Week 2 is the lightest at about 75 minutes a night. Family week is the heaviest at about 94, holding two of the four films over 100 minutes.

## Which of the 31 films are public domain?

The US Copyright Office's [Circular 15a on copyright duration](https://www.copyright.gov/circs/circ15a.pdf), revised April 2026, states that all works published in the United States before 1 January 1931 are in the public domain. That covers all six week-1 films, and archive.org hosts copies of each.

The same circular caps older works at 95 years, counted from the end of the year copyright was secured. By that arithmetic *Dracula* and *Frankenstein*, both 1931, enter the US public domain on 1 January 2027, so October 2027 has eight public-domain nights against six in 2026. Restorations and new scores can carry their own copyright.

*Night of the Living Dead* is usually listed as public domain, and archive.org hosts a [1080p copy marked public domain](https://archive.org/details/Night.Of.The.Living.Dead_1080p). But the [AFI Catalog's history note](https://catalog.afi.com/Catalog/moviedetails/19843), citing Variety of 2 May 1990, says the retitled film lost its copyright and Image Ten secured a new one in 1986. For the other 23 films, catalogues change monthly and by country, so check a JustWatch-type tracker on the day.

## Why one film a night beats a weekend marathon

A 2017 First Monday study by Horvath and colleagues [split 51 University of Melbourne students into weekly, daily and one-sitting viewing of six TV episodes](https://firstmonday.org/ojs/index.php/fm/article/view/7729). The one-sitting group scored well the day after, but their memories faded faster across tests at 7 and 140 days, and they reported significantly less enjoyment.

Sleep is the second cost. A 2017 Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine survey of 423 adults aged 18 to 25 linked [more frequent binge viewing to poorer sleep quality, more fatigue and more insomnia symptoms](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC5529125), while regular TV viewing showed no such link, and mental arousal before sleep explained it. Both measured TV series, not films, so read them as a case for one film a night, not proof about horror.

## Sharing the calendar with one person

SubhSandesh pages average 11.1 views each, which suggests a page carrying the plan gets reopened. These are one-person greeting pages, not a watch-party tool, and neither plays a film.

For a weeknight nudge, the [interactive Halloween card with a pumpkin to carve](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about 5 minutes: up to six photos, a letter read by flashlight, and a jack-o'-lantern that glows with your chosen word, such as tonight's title. Its No button runs away, so send it only to someone who has already said yes.

For the person watching all 31 with you, the [premium cinematic Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about 10 minutes and adds a voice note up to 60 seconds, up to 12 photos and an optional unlock time, so it can open on 31 October after *Halloween* ends. Their one reply, up to 280 characters, is emailed to you.

To ask someone to join before 1 October, [The Invitation page](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) fits better than either Halloween page. They must answer it, and a yes turns into a countdown to your start date.

## When this calendar is the wrong plan

Young children should skip weeks 3 and 5, where AFI lists 8 of the 12 films as R. Family week alone, six nights from 19 to 24 October, is the safer slice for under-10s.

Silent intertitles are hard to read on a small screen, and 48.3% of views on our shared pages happen on a phone, so put week 1 on a television. A printed list on the fridge beats any link for some households, and our pages are English only.

## Sources

- Horvath et al., First Monday, 1 September 2017.
- Exelmans and Van den Bulck, J Clin Sleep Med, August 2017.
- US Copyright Office, Circular 15a, revised April 2026.
- AFI Catalog, *Night of the Living Dead* entry.
- Library of Congress, [National Film Registry listing](https://www.loc.gov/programs/national-film-preservation-board/film-registry/complete-national-film-registry-listing/), undated.
- Internet Archive, *Night of the Living Dead* item.
